stories.title: AIPAC Is Spending Millions — Just Not Under Its Own Name
stories.text: The money bomb dropped out of nowhere. In February 2026, weeks before Illinois’ Democratic primary races, two newly formed political action committees (PACs) began unleashing millions in the race for the state’s 9th Congressional District, which includes parts of Chicago. Named Elect Chicago Women and Chicago Progressive Partnership, the groups deployed attack ads against two candidates: Daniel Biss, former mayor of Evanston, Illinois, and political newcomer Kat Abughazaleh. NEW - Dark money super PAC Elect Chicago Women goes negative on Daniel Biss in a new ad #IL09 pic.twitter.com/aqDtScISNl — Matthew Eadie (@mattheweadie22) February 21, 2026 The operations were utterly opaque. The brand-new entities had no obvious ties to prominent politicians or interest groups, and their filing paperwork had been wiped of any clues identifying their backers. The groups timed their operations — when they started fundraising and bankrolling ads — so that they wouldn’t have to file anything disclosing their donors until after the March 17 election.
